artboards.title: Records search — at rest, with coverage before any query
One query, two legs, and the three ways it comes back short
The defect, the closed outcome vocabulary, and what is not settled

annotations.text:
COVERAGE BEFORE RESULTS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE SURFACE.
This finder owns no records. It reads eleven registered regions and one corpus, and it can read neither completely: one region has its vendor withheld on the pack this is drawn on, and the corpus is scope-bound and partly unsearchable.
So a result count on this page is never printed alone. The coverage panel goes first, with one row per leg, and the corpus leg carries the product's own counts plus the counting rule verbatim from emptyCoverage(). "We found 2" and "we searched 10 of 11 regions and 25 of 28 documents" are different sentences, and only the second one is true.

A ZERO IS THE MOST DANGEROUS THING THIS PAGE CAN PRINT.
There are three ways this search comes back short and only one of them is "no matches". A region whose gating adapter is not granted was not asked. A scope the reader does not hold is refused with the product's own code, read_outside_scope. A document with no text layer under it cannot be searched, and the product records why.
Rendering any of those as an empty list tells the reader the records do not exist. That is a false statement about the city, made in the one place a city is most likely to believe it.

EVERY WORD ON THIS SURFACE IS ALREADY THE PRODUCT'S.
Outcomes are the four composer statuses plus the read refusal code plus the two counts named in the product's own counting rule — seven words, derived in dump-source-state.mjs rather than declared here.
Document states are the product's five, and its reasons are its three. reason-not-recorded is a STATE and never a REASON: the product's own CHECK constraint refuses it as a stored value, and check.mjs refuses to let the two lists merge.
A finder that can invent an outcome word can invent "we searched everything", which is the one sentence this surface must not be able to say when it has not.

THIS SURFACE IS NOT "NOT BUILT", AND THE DESIGN SAYS SO CAREFULLY.
src/domains.mjs closed that phrase at one meaning: absent from DOMAIN_REGISTRY. Records search is absent from the registry for a reason that is not the same as Parks — it generates no records of its own, so it has nothing to register rather than no vendor to gate it.
That is why the boards quote the shipped stub verbatim inside data-stub="today" and allow the words "Not built" nowhere else but the shipped nav. The stub is a quote of what a city sees today. It is not this design's verdict on the page it draws.

TWO REGISTER ROWS, AND NEITHER IS THIS SURFACE'S SUBJECT.
The register says "Prophecy document search → Work Records search (Not built)" and "City document table → Files (Island)". The first is a retired product's function, not a design brief; the second is a table of documents that already has a home on the Files mount.
So this surface is not the city document table moved sideways. It is the finder that resolves across the two homes a document-adjacent record can be in, and the acceptance items board names the three things owed before it can ship: the third noun in the chrome, the origin the corpus sits behind, and which scope a staff reader's search reads.
